idiom_name: tagged union: struct with an enum discriminant, an anonymous union payload, opaque constructor and accessor functions
implementation_notes: The classic C realization is a struct holding an enum tag plus an anonymous union of per-state payload structs, documented and enforced by convention: construction goes through functions such as connection_connect(), access through a switch on the tag, and the struct is kept opaque in the header so callers cannot set the tag and the payload inconsistently. C99 designated initializers keep the constructors readable, and the accessor functions return a failure value (NULL) when they are called for a state whose payload is not live. What replaces the sealed structure is the discipline of the accessor layer: reading a union member other than the one last stored is undefined behaviour, and only -Wswitch (ideally with -Werror=switch) makes the compiler notice a new enumerator that some switch forgot. Where the state has no per-state payload, prefer a plain enum plus a switch and skip the union entirely.
pitfalls: Reading a union member other than the one last stored is undefined behaviour: the tag and the payload must be written together by one constructor, and every read must go through a tag-checked accessor.
The enum tag is an ordinary integer: anything can assign an out-of-range or mismatched value unless the struct is opaque and the only setters are the package's own constructors.
switch statements over the enum are not exhaustiveness-checked by default - compile with -Wswitch and treat the warning as an error, or a new state is silently ignored.
